Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
The failing test `testSingleOptionMaximumNumberOfArgument` sets up an option `-b` with a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 4 arguments, and default values of 100, 1000, and 10000. It then parses an array `args` with values `["-b", "1", "2"]` and expects the parsed values of the `-b` option to be `"[1, 2, 10000]"`.

The current bug report describes that when using multiple arguments and default values, the behavior is counter-intuitive and defaults are only picked up if no arguments are passed in. The user expects the behavior to be consistent based on the argument count and defaults provided.

Looking at the code snippets, the method `org.apache.commons.cli2.builder.DefaultOptionBuilder.withArgument` is used to set the argument for the option, and `org.apache.commons.cli2.builder.ArgumentBuilder.withName` is used to set the name for the argument. The `org.apache.commons.cli2.builder.GroupBuilder.create` method is used to create a group of options.

The issue might be related to how the defaults are handled when parsing arguments with the `-b` option in the test case. It seems that the default values are not being considered when arguments are provided, leading to unexpected behavior.

To fix this issue, it is likely that adjustments need to be made in the parsing logic to properly handle default values when arguments are provided. 

Here are the methods that could be fixed:
1. `org.apache.commons.cli2.builder.DefaultOptionBuilder.withArgument(org.apache.commons.cli2.Argument)`
2. `org.apache.commons.cli2.builder.ArgumentBuilder.withName(java.lang.String)`

These methods are involved in setting up the options and arguments, which might need modifications to ensure the default values are correctly utilized during parsing.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
